newsitem.title: USA: FBI official pleads guilty in Ruby Ridge case.
newsitem.headline: FBI official pleads guilty in Ruby Ridge case.

text.p: An FBI official pleaded guilty Wednesday to a single obstruction of justice charge for concealing and destroying an internal review of the deadly 1992 shootout in Ruby Ridge, Idaho.

E. Michael Kahoe, former chief of the FBI's violent crimes section, admitted his role in keeping from U.S. prosecutors the review they needed to prepare for the murder trial of white separatist Randy Weaver -- the key figure in the Ruby Ridge affair.
U.S. District Judge Ricardo Urbina accepted the guilty plea and told Kahoe he faced a maximum possible punishment of 10 years in prison. No date was set for sentencing.

Prosecutor Eric Sitarchuk told the judge Kahoe has agreed to cooperate with the long-running criminal investigation into whether FBI officials had engaged in wrongdoing or a possible cover-up involving the controversial shootout.

Sitarchuk said Kahoe destroyed the review because the "FBI had problems with the Weaver case" and did not want prosecutors or defense attorneys to know it. Weaver eventually was acquitted of the murder charges.

Sitarchuk said Kahoe took all his copies of the review and threw them into his "confidential trash can" where they were shredded, and he then directed a subordinate to do the same and "make it appear as if it never existed."
